verses.1: For the music director. A psalm of David.
verses.2: May the LORD answer you in the day of distress; may the name of the God of Jacob protect you.
verses.3: May he send help from his holy dwelling and support you from Zion.
verses.4: May he remember all your offerings and accept your burnt offerings. Selah.
verses.5: May he grant you what you desire and fulfill all your plans.
verses.6: We will rejoice in your salvation, and in the name of our God we will exult. May the LORD fulfill all your requests.
verses.7: Now I know that the LORD has saved his anointed one; he answers him from his holy sky, with mighty strength from his right hand.
verses.8: Some are on horses and some on chariots, but we will call on the name of the LORD our God.
verses.9: They collapse and fall, but we rise up and are steadfast.
verses.10: LORD, save the king; answer us when we call.

notes:
Notes  
- v. 4: "Selah" is preserved as in the text.  
- v. 7: "his holy sky" reflects "שְׁמֵי קָדְשׁוֹ" as "heaven of his holiness" or "holy sky."  
- v. 8: "on horses and on chariots" is a standard way of describing military might; the contrast with calling on the LORD is intentional.  
- v. 10: "the king" is not explicitly named, so the term is used directly as in the Hebrew.
